I'm sitting here at the kitchen table thinking about this year like I do every spring. My 12 mu — I've been working this land a long time. Cotton is my main crop, always has been. Most of my land, about 10 mu, I'll put in cotton again. The other 2 mu I keep for wheat in winter and maize in summer — that way we have our own flour and some corn for the chickens and to sell a bit.

For cotton, I'll plant the improved Bt variety like last year. The seeds cost more but the bollworm doesn't eat them up. I buy from the same dealer in town, he sells the kind my neighbors use. I'll put down about 40 jin of compound fertilizer per mu before planting — that's 15-15-15 — and then top-dress with urea twice, maybe 20 jin each time at budding and flowering. So pure nitrogen comes out around 16-17 kg per mu, phosphorus about 6, potassium about 6. Cotton drinks water — I irrigate 3 times from my well: once before planting, once at flowering, once when the bolls are filling. Pests are the real worry — aphids early, then bollworm, mites in hot weather. I spray 6 times usually. Can't skip or I lose the crop. Last year I got about 250 kg of seed cotton per mu, I hope for the same.

For wheat on the 2 mu, I follow what we always do here. Plant Jimai variety in October. Base fertilizer compound 50 jin, then urea top-dress in spring. That's about 14 kg N, 7 kg P, 5 kg K. Water 3 times — winter, green-up, filling. Spray twice for aphids and rust. I get around 450 kg per mu.

For maize after wheat, I plant Zhengdan hybrid. Less fussy crop. About 15 kg N, 5 kg P, 5 kg K. Two irrigations, two sprays. Usually 500 kg per mu.

Cotton takes most of my money for pesticide. Wheat and maize are cheaper to grow but prices are low. I don't change much — what worked last year will work this year if the weather is decent.
